subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Nanotechnology: Engineering the Invisible
description: A quick win: understand Nanotechnology: Engineering the Invisible.

hook.text: In 1959, Richard Feynman gave a talk titled 'There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom.' He imagined machines built atom by atom.

buildup.text: In 1981, the scanning tunneling microscope let scientists see individual atoms for the first time.

discovery.text: IBM researchers used the same tool to spell 'IBM' with 35 xenon atoms. They moved matter one atom at a time.

twist.text: Today, nano-coatings repel water and bacteria. They protect phone screens, medical tools, and spacecraft.

climax.text: Engineers are designing nano-robots to deliver drugs inside the body, targeting cancer cells directly.

punchline.text: The next engineering frontier isn't bigger. It's smaller.

quiz.question: What did IBM researchers famously do with a scanning tunneling microscope?
options: They photographed a single water molecule in motion
They spelled 'IBM' by moving 35 individual xenon atoms
They split an atom to release nuclear energy
